definition: A resource that cannot be replaced once used up — it will eventually run out. Fossil fuels and metals are examples.
clues: This is a type of natural resource
It cannot be replaced once used
Fossil fuels and metals are examples
A resource that exists in limited amounts and will eventually run out — e.g. coal, oil, copper, iron ore

definition: A resource that can be replaced at the same rate it is used, so it will not run out. Examples: timber, solar energy, wind.
clues: This is a type of natural resource
It can be replenished at the same rate it is used
Solar energy and timber are examples
A resource that is naturally replaced as fast as it is consumed — e.g. solar energy, wind, sustainably harvested timber

definition: Development that meets current needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
clues: This is a concept in resource management
It considers the needs of future generations
It balances economic development with environmental protection
Meeting today's resource needs without preventing future generations from meeting theirs — a key goal of environmental policy

definition: An analysis of the environmental impact of a product throughout its entire life — from obtaining raw materials through manufacture, use and disposal.
clues: This is an analysis technique for products
It considers every stage of a product's life
It is used to compare the environmental impact of different products
An evaluation of a product's environmental impact from raw material extraction to disposal — used to make more sustainable choices

definition: Water that is safe to drink — it is not pure water, but has low enough levels of dissolved substances and microbes to be safe for consumption.
clues: This is a term for a specific type of water
It is safe to drink
It is not chemically pure water
Water with safe levels of dissolved substances and microbes — not chemically pure, but clean enough to drink without harm

definition: The process of making water safe to drink, including sedimentation, filtration and chlorination.
clues: This is a process to make water safe
It involves several stages
Filtration and chlorination are two steps
The stages of making drinking water: sedimentation (solid settling), filtration (removing particles), chlorination (killing microbes)

definition: The first stage of water treatment where large solid particles settle to the bottom of a tank under gravity.
clues: This is a stage of water treatment
Large solid particles fall to the bottom of a tank
It uses gravity
The first stage of water treatment — solid particles in the water settle out under gravity before filtration begins

definition: A stage of water treatment where water is passed through layers of sand and gravel to remove smaller particles.
clues: This is a stage of water treatment
Water is passed through sand and gravel
It removes small particles from the water
Water is passed through gravel and sand beds — smaller particles that didn't settle are trapped as the water filters through

definition: The final stage of water treatment where chlorine is added to kill any remaining microorganisms and make the water safe to drink.
clues: This is a stage of water treatment
Chlorine is added to the water
It kills microorganisms
Chlorine is added at the final stage of water treatment — it kills bacteria and other microbes, making water safe to drink

definition: The process of removing dissolved salts from seawater to produce fresh water. Methods include distillation and reverse osmosis.
clues: This is a process to produce fresh water
It removes dissolved salts from seawater
Distillation and reverse osmosis are two methods
Removing salt from seawater to produce drinking water — expensive and energy-intensive, used in water-scarce regions

definition: A method of desalination where high pressure forces seawater through a semi-permeable membrane, removing dissolved salts.
clues: This is a method used in desalination
High pressure is applied to seawater
A semi-permeable membrane is used
High pressure forces seawater through a membrane that blocks salt ions — producing clean, drinkable fresh water

definition: The gradual destruction of a metal by chemical reactions with its environment, such as oxidation by oxygen and water.
clues: This is a process that damages metals
It involves chemical reactions with the environment
Rusting is the most common example
The chemical degradation of metals due to reactions with oxygen and water — rusting (iron) and verdigris (copper) are examples

definition: A mixture of a metal with one or more other elements (usually metals). Alloys have different and often improved properties compared to pure metals.
clues: This is a type of material made from metals
It is a mixture of a metal with other elements
Steel and bronze are examples
A mixture of a metal with other elements — alloying changes the properties, often making the material stronger or more resistant to corrosion

definition: An alloy of iron and carbon. Different types (e.g. stainless steel) have different properties depending on the proportion of carbon and other metals added.
clues: This is an alloy of iron
It contains iron and carbon
Stainless steel is a well-known type
An alloy of iron and carbon — adding chromium makes stainless steel; varying carbon content changes hardness and brittleness

definition: An alloy of copper and tin. Harder than copper and used in tools, weapons and statues.
clues: This is an alloy of copper and tin
It is harder than copper alone
It was used extensively in prehistoric tools and weapons
A copper-tin alloy — harder and more durable than pure copper, historically used for tools, weapons and coins

definition: An alloy of copper and zinc. Used in musical instruments, plumbing fittings and door handles because of its attractive appearance and corrosion resistance.
clues: This is an alloy of copper and zinc
It is used in musical instruments and plumbing
It is harder than copper
A copper-zinc alloy — attractive golden colour, corrosion resistant, used in musical instruments, valves and fittings

definition: Non-metallic solids made from clay or other inorganic materials, baked at high temperatures. Hard and brittle, with high melting points.
clues: This is a type of material
It is made from clay or inorganic materials
It is hard, brittle and has a high melting point
Materials made by firing clay or inorganic compounds at high temperature — hard and brittle, used in pottery, bricks and electronics

definition: A material made from two or more different materials that together have better properties than either component alone. Examples: fibreglass, concrete, carbon fibre reinforced polymer.
clues: This is a type of material made from two or more components
The combination gives better properties than either component alone
Fibreglass and concrete are examples
Two or more materials combined to exploit the best properties of each — e.g. fibreglass (glass fibres in resin), carbon fibre composites

definition: The process of converting used materials or waste into new products to reduce the use of raw materials and energy.
clues: This is an environmental process
It converts used materials into new products
It conserves raw materials and reduces waste
Processing used or waste materials to make new products — reduces the need for mining raw materials and lowers energy consumption

definition: Copper can be extracted from low-grade ores using phytomining (plants absorb copper) or bioleaching (bacteria dissolve copper compounds), then purified by electrolysis.
clues: This describes methods of obtaining a specific metal from low-grade sources
Phytomining and bioleaching are two modern methods
Plants or bacteria are involved in these processes
Modern methods for low-grade copper ores: plants absorb copper (phytomining) or bacteria dissolve it (bioleaching) — greener alternatives to traditional mining

definition: A technique where plants are grown on low-grade metal ore. The plants absorb the metal, are then burned, and the metal is extracted from the ash.
clues: This is a method used to extract metals
Plants are used to absorb the metal from soil
The plants are then burned to recover the metal
Plants grown on metal-rich soil absorb the metal — burning the plant produces ash from which the metal can be extracted

definition: A technique where bacteria are used to convert insoluble metal compounds into soluble ones, which can then be extracted from the resulting solution.
clues: This is a method used to extract metals from low-grade ores
Bacteria are used in this process
Insoluble metal compounds are converted to soluble ones
Bacteria break down low-grade ore and release metal ions into solution — the metal is then recovered from the leachate

definition: Water is hard if it contains dissolved calcium or magnesium ions, which prevent soap from lathering and form scale in pipes and boilers.
clues: This is a property of some types of water
It is caused by dissolved calcium or magnesium ions
It prevents soap from lathering easily
Water containing Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺ ions — it forms scum with soap and scale in pipes and boilers; can be temporary or permanent

definition: Hardness caused by dissolved calcium hydrogen carbonate — removed by boiling, which decomposes it and forms calcium carbonate scale.
clues: This is a type of hard water
It can be removed by boiling
It is caused by dissolved calcium hydrogen carbonate
Hard water caused by Ca(HCO₃)₂ — boiling causes it to decompose, depositing calcium carbonate (limescale) and softening the water

definition: Hardness caused by dissolved calcium sulfate — cannot be removed by boiling; must be removed using ion exchange or by adding washing soda.
clues: This is a type of hard water
Boiling does not remove it
It is caused by dissolved calcium sulfate
Hard water caused by CaSO₄ — cannot be removed by boiling; requires ion exchange resin or addition of sodium carbonate (washing soda)

definition: A material used to soften hard water by exchanging Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions with Na⁺ or H⁺ ions, removing the hardness.
clues: This is a material used in water softening
It swaps calcium and magnesium ions for harmless ones
It is found in water softeners and dishwashers
A resin that removes Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions from hard water, replacing them with Na⁺ or H⁺ ions — used in water softeners
